gaps.sentence: We owe our success to her ___ (VISION) leadership.
The results of the survey were highly ___ (SURPRISE).
The problem was ___ (SIMPLE) a matter of bad timing.
gaps.explanation: 'Simply a matter of' = only a matter of.
'Highly suspicious' — the adjective for something that looks wrong.

gaps.sentence: They're ___ (HOPE) that the talks will resume.
gaps.explanation: 'Be hopeful that…' = feeling hope; 'hopefully' is the adverb.

gaps.sentence: The factory will ___ (EMPLOY) fifty more workers next year.
gaps.explanation: The bare verb follows 'will': will employ.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (REFUSE) to cooperate stalled the negotiations.
The report was highly ___ (CRITIC) of the new scheme.
gaps.explanation: 'Highly critical of' — the adjective describing a judgement.
